# Shannon-Weiner index {#sec-shannon}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}
$$
    H = - \sum_{i = 1}^S p_i \ln p_i
$${#eq-shannon}
$$
    H = \ln \frac{1}{\prod_{i = 1}^S p_i^{p_i}}
$${#eq-shannon-alt}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

### Shannon index with dune data

Using the classic `dune` dataset from the `vegan` package:

```{r}
library(vegan)
data(dune)

# Calculate Shannon index for each site
shannon <- diversity(dune, index = "shannon")
shannon
```

This calculates the Shannon biodiversity index for each of the 20 sites in the dune dataset. The `diversity()` function from `vegan` computes:
$$H = - \sum_{i = 1}^S p_i \ln p_i$$

where $p_i$ is the proportion of species $i$ relative to all species at that site.

You can also extract specific sites or summarize the results:

```{r}
# Shannon index for the first site
shannon[1]

# Summary statistics across all sites
summary(shannon)

# Visual comparison across sites
barplot(shannon, main = "Shannon Diversity Index - Dune Sites",
        xlab = "Site", ylab = "Shannon Index")
```

Higher Shannon index values indicate greater species diversity (both more species and more even distribution).
